name: Split Backs
summary: Two backs split behind the quarterback and the SL out wide. One fewer back than a three-back look, and the receiver out there blocks the corner the pitch has to get around.
personnel: 11 players, 2 tight ends, quarterback, 2 halfbacks, 1 SL split out
notes: Both ends are tight on the line. The two backs sit four yards deep and just over two yards either side of the quarterback, one behind each guard–tackle gap — same depth, same split, so the alignment gives nothing away. The slot is off the line and split out wide, which keeps seven on the line. The 3-back is always the left halfback (odd holes) and the 2-back is always the right halfback (even holes). The call names the slot's side every time — Slot Right or Slot Left.
